children.text: lokātīta namas tubhyaṃ viviktajñānavedine |
children.translated_text: Homage to you, O Transcender of the World (<s>Lokātīta</s>), knower of solitary wisdom,

children.text: yas tvaṃ jagaddhitāyaiva khinnaḥ karuṇayā ciram || NagLok_01
children.translated_text: you who, for the welfare of the world alone, have long been wearied by compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). || 1 ||

children.text: skandhamātravinirmukto na sattvo 'stīti te matam |
children.translated_text: Released from the mere aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), it is your view that no being (<s>sattva</s>) exists;

children.text: sattvārthaṃ ca paraṃ khedam agamas tvaṃ mahāmune || NagLok_02
children.translated_text: yet for the sake of beings you underwent the utmost hardship, O Great Sage (<s>Mahāmuni</s>). || 2 ||

children.text: te 'pi skandhās tvayā dhīman dhīmadbhyaḥ saṃprakāśitāḥ |
children.translated_text: Those very aggregates, O Wise One, you have illuminated for the wise

children.text: māyāmarīcigandharvanagarasvapnasaṃnibhāḥ || NagLok_03
children.translated_text: as resembling illusions (<s>māyā</s>), mirages, <s>Gandharva</s> cities, and dreams. || 3 ||

children.text: hetutaḥ saṃbhavo yeṣāṃ tadabhāvān na santi ye |
children.translated_text: Those which arise from causes and which do not exist in the absence of those [causes] —

children.text: kathaṃ nāma na te spaṣṭaṃ pratibimbasamā matāḥ || NagLok_04
children.translated_text: how are they not clearly regarded by you as similar to reflections? || 4 ||

children.text: bhūtāny acakṣurgrāhyāṇi tanmayaṃ cākṣuṣaṃ katham |
children.translated_text: The elements (<s>bhūtas</s>) are not grasped by the eye; how then can the visible

children.text: rūpaṃ tvayaivaṃ bruvatā rūpagrāho nivāritaḥ || NagLok_05
children.translated_text: form (<s>rūpa</s>), which is made of them, [be so grasped]? By speaking thus, you have prevented the grasping of form. || 5 ||

children.text: vedanīyaṃ vinā nāsti vedanāto nirātmikā |
children.translated_text: Without something to be felt, feeling (<s>vedanā</s>) does not exist; therefore it is without self (<s>nirātmikā</s>).

children.text: tac ca vedyaṃ svabhāvena nāstīty abhimataṃ tava || NagLok_06
children.translated_text: And that which is to be felt does not exist by its own nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) — such is your view. || 6 ||

children.text: saṃjñārthayor ananyatve mukhaṃ dahyeta vahninā |
children.translated_text: If perception (<s>saṃjñā</s>) and its object were non-different, the mouth would be burned by fire;

children.text: anyatve 'dhigamābhāvas tvayoktaṃ bhūtavādinā || NagLok_07
children.translated_text: if different, there would be no apprehension — so you, the speaker of truth (<s>bhūtavādin</s>), have stated. || 7 ||

children.text: kartā svatantraḥ karmāpi tvayoktaṃ vyavahārataḥ |
children.translated_text: The agent is autonomous, and so is action (<s>karma</s>) — thus you have spoken in conventional terms;

children.text: parasparāpekṣikī tu siddhis te 'bhimatānayoḥ || NagLok_08
children.translated_text: but their establishment is mutually dependent (<s>parasparāpekṣikī</s>) — such is your accepted [view] of these two. || 8 ||

children.text: na kartāsti na bhoktāsti puṇyāpuṇyaṃ pratītyajam |
children.translated_text: There is no agent and no experiencer; merit and demerit arise dependently (<s>pratītyaja</s>).

children.text: yat pratītya na taj jātaṃ proktaṃ vācaspate tvayā || NagLok_09
children.translated_text: That which arises dependently has not [truly] arisen — so you, O Lord of Speech (<s>Vācaspati</s>), have declared. || 9 ||

children.text: ajñāyamānaṃ na jñeyaṃ vijñānaṃ tad vinā na ca |
children.translated_text: Without being known, there is no knowable object; and without that [knowable], there is no consciousness (<s>vijñāna</s>).

children.text: tasmāt svabhāvato na sto jñānajñeye tvam ūcivān || NagLok_10
children.translated_text: Therefore, knowledge and the knowable do not exist by their own nature — so you have stated. || 10 ||

children.text: lakṣyāl lakṣaṇam anyac cet syāt tal lakṣyam alakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: If the characteristic (<s>lakṣaṇa</s>) were other than the characterized (<s>lakṣya</s>), the characterized would be without characteristics;

children.text: tayor abhāvo 'nanyatve vispaṣṭaṃ kathitaṃ tvayā || NagLok_11
children.translated_text: and the non-existence of both [results] if they are non-different — this you have clearly stated. || 11 ||

children.text: lakṣyalakṣaṇanirmuktaṃ vāgudāhāravarjitam |
children.translated_text: Free from the characterized and the characteristic, beyond the reach of verbal expression —

children.text: śāntaṃ jagad idaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhavatā jñānacakṣuṣā || NagLok_12
children.translated_text: this world is peaceful — so has been seen by you with the eye of wisdom (<s>jñānacakṣus</s>). || 12 ||

children.text: na sann utpadyate bhāvo nāpy asan sadasan na ca |
children.translated_text: An existent entity does not arise, nor does a non-existent one, nor one both existent and non-existent;

children.text: na svato nāpi parato na dvābhyāṃ jāyate katham || NagLok_13
children.translated_text: not from itself, not from another, not from both — how then is anything born? || 13 ||

children.text: na sataḥ sthitiyuktasya vināśa upapadyate |
children.translated_text: For an existent entity endowed with persistence, destruction is not tenable;

children.text: nāsato 'śvaviṣāṇena samasya śamatā katham || NagLok_14
children.translated_text: for a non-existent one, equal to a horse's horn — how can there be cessation? || 14 ||

children.text: bhāvān nārthāntaraṃ nāśo nāpy anarthāntaraṃ matam |
children.translated_text: Destruction is held to be neither a different thing from the entity nor a non-different thing;

children.text: arthāntare bhaven nityo nāpy anarthāntare bhavet || NagLok_15
children.translated_text: if different, it would be eternal; if non-different, it would not exist [at all]. || 15 ||

children.text: ekatve na hi bhāvasya vināśa upapadyate |
children.translated_text: In the case of identity, the destruction of an entity is not tenable;

children.text: pṛthaktve na hi bhāvasya vināśa upapadyate || NagLok_16
children.translated_text: in the case of difference, the destruction of an entity is not tenable. || 16 ||

children.text: vinaṣṭāt kāraṇāt tāvat kāryotpattir na yujyate |
children.translated_text: From a destroyed cause, the arising of an effect is not justified;

children.text: na cāvinaṣṭāt svapnena tulyotpattir matā tava || NagLok_17
children.translated_text: nor from an undestroyed one — arising is held by you to be like a dream. || 17 ||

children.text: na niruddhān nāniruddhād bījād aṅkurasaṃbhavaḥ |
children.translated_text: Not from a ceased seed, nor from an unceased one, does the sprout arise;

children.text: māyotpādavad utpādaḥ sarva eva tvayocyate || NagLok_18
children.translated_text: all arising is declared by you to be like the arising of an illusion (<s>māyā</s>). || 18 ||

children.text: atas tvayā jagad idaṃ parikalpasamudbhavam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, this world, arising from conceptual construction (<s>parikalpa</s>),

children.text: parijñātam asadbhūtam anutpannam na naśyati || NagLok_19
children.translated_text: has been thoroughly understood by you as unreal, unborn, and not subject to destruction. || 19 ||

children.text: nityasya saṃsṛtir nāsti naivānityasya saṃsṛtiḥ |
children.translated_text: For the permanent there is no <s>saṃsāra</s> (cyclic existence), and for the impermanent there is no <s>saṃsāra</s> either;

children.text: svapnavat saṃsṛtiḥ proktā tvayā tattvavidāṃ vara || NagLok_20
children.translated_text: <s>saṃsāra</s> is declared by you, O best of knowers of reality, to be like a dream. || 20 ||

children.text: svayaṃkṛtaṃ parakṛtaṃ dvābhyāṃ kṛtam ahetukam |
children.translated_text: Self-made, other-made, made by both, or without cause —

children.text: tārkikair iṣyate duḥkhaṃ tvayā tūktaṃ pratītyajam || NagLok_21
children.translated_text: suffering is accepted [in these ways] by the logicians; but you have declared it to be dependently arisen (<s>pratītyaja</s>). || 21 ||

children.text: yaḥ pratītyasamutpādaḥ śūnyatā saiva te matā |
children.translated_text: That which is dependent origination (<s>pratītyasamutpāda</s>) — that itself is <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness), in your view.

children.text: bhāvaḥ svatantro nāstīti siṃhanādas tavātulaḥ || NagLok_22
children.translated_text: 'There is no independently existing entity' — this is your incomparable lion's roar (<s>siṃhanāda</s>). || 22 ||

children.text: sarvasaṃkalpanāśāya śūnyatāmṛtadeśanā |
children.translated_text: For the destruction of all conceptual constructions, you taught the nectar of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness);

children.text: yasya tasyām api grāhas tvayāsāv avasāditaḥ || NagLok_23
children.translated_text: yet whoever grasps even at that [emptiness] has been censured by you. || 23 ||

children.text: nirīhā vaśikāḥ śūnyā māyāvat pratyayodbhavāḥ |
children.translated_text: Without effort, subject to conditions, empty, arisen from conditions, like illusions —

children.text: sarvadharmās tvayā nātha niḥsvabhāvāḥ prakāśitāḥ || NagLok_24
children.translated_text: all <s>dharmas</s> (phenomena) have been revealed by you, O Protector (<s>Nātha</s>), as devoid of own-nature (<s>niḥsvabhāva</s>). || 24 ||

children.text: na tvayotpāditaṃ kiṃ cin na ca kiṃ cin nirodhitam |
children.translated_text: Nothing whatsoever has been produced by you, and nothing whatsoever has been ceased;

children.text: yathā pūrvaṃ tathā paścāt tathatāṃ buddhavān asi || NagLok_25
children.translated_text: as before, so after — you have realized <s>tathatā</s> (suchness, thusness). || 25 ||

children.text: āryair nisevitām enām anāgamya hi bhāvanām |
children.translated_text: Without resorting to this meditation (<s>bhāvanā</s>) cultivated by the Noble Ones (<s>āryas</s>),

children.text: nānimittam hi vijñānaṃ bhavatīha kathaṃ cana || NagLok_26
children.translated_text: consciousness without characteristics (<s>animiṭṭa</s>) does not arise here in any way. || 26 ||

children.text: animittam anāgamya mokṣo nāsti tvam uktavān |
children.translated_text: Without attaining the signless (<s>animitta</s>), there is no liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>) — so you have stated;

children.text: atas tvayā mahāyāne tat sākalyena deśitam || NagLok_27
children.translated_text: therefore you have taught that in its entirety in the <s>Mahāyāna</s> (Great Vehicle). || 27 ||

children.text: yad avāptaṃ mayā puṇyaṃ stutvā tvāṃ stutibhājanam |
children.translated_text: Whatever merit I have obtained by praising you, who are worthy of praise,

children.text: nimittabandhanāpetaṃ bhūyāt tenākhilaṃ yagat || NagLok_28
children.translated_text: may the entire world, by that [merit], become free from the bondage of characteristics (<s>nimitta</s>). || 28 ||

body.translated_text: Thus the <s>Lokātītastava</s> (Hymn to the Transcender of the World) is complete.
